The arc length of a curve y=f(x) between x=a and x=b can be found using the formula L=∫ab1+[f′(x)]2dx.

In our case, f(x)=x36+12x, a=1, and b=2.

First, we find the derivative of f(x): f′(x)=3x26−12x2=x4−12x2

Now, let's compute 1+[f′(x)]2:

Substituting f′(x)=x4−12x2 to the formula for the arc length, we get 1+[f′(x)]2=1+(x4−12x2)2=1+x8−2x4+14x4=4x4+x8−2x4+14x4=x8+2x4+14x4=(x4+1)24x4=x4+12x2=12(x2+x−2)

Substituting 1+[f′(x)]2=12(x2+x−2) to the formula for the arc length, we get L=12∫12(x2+x−2)dx=12[13x3−x−1]|12=12[(13⋅23−2−1)−(13⋅13−1−1))=12[83−12−13+1]=1712.
